title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. Reimplementation of the method described in
"Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data"
(arXiv:2510.13352), Sections 4.1-4.3.

Pipeline
--------
1. Equal-frequency binning (Eq. 4): for each feature j the ``nbins`` bin
   centers are evenly-spaced percentiles of the *observed* values only,
   ``c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1) * 100 / (nbins - 1))``, so that
   ``c_{j,1}``/``c_{j,nbins}`` are the min/max of the feature.
2. Proximity assignment (Eq. 5): every observed value goes to its nearest
   center (Voronoi cell); ties break to the lowest bin index.
3. One-hot encoding (Eqs. 6-7): ``h_{i,j}`` is a one-hot vector over bins and
   ``z_i`` is the concatenation over features.
4. Cascading fallback for missing entries (Eqs. 8-14): level 1 = mean one-hot
   over samples matching on *all* observed features of i (intersection),
   level 2 = mean one-hot over samples matching on *any* observed feature
   (union), level 3 = global prior bin frequencies.
5. Proximity kernel (Eq. 15): ``K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n``.
"""
import numpy as np


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. equal-frequency binning
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def fit_bins(X, nbins, center_mode="paper_eq4"):
    """Compute bin centers and global priors for every feature.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : (n, d) float array with NaN for missing values.
    nbins : int, number of bins per feature.
    center_mode : str

        ``"midpoint"``   -> percentiles 100*k/(nbins+1) (interior quantiles).

        feature j has no observed value.
    priors : (d, nbins) array of global bin probabilities (Eq. 13).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    n, d = X.shape
    centers = []
    priors = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            continue
        if center_mode == "paper_eq4":
            pct = 100.0 * np.arange(nbins) / (nbins - 1) if nbins > 1 else np.array([50.0])
        elif center_mode == "midpoint":
            pct = 100.0 * (np.arange(1, nbins + 1)) / (nbins + 1)
        else:
            raise ValueError(center_mode)
        c = np.percentile(obs, pct, method="linear")
        centers.append(c)
        # global prior: frequency of each bin among observed values (Eq. 13)
        b = np.argmin(np.abs(obs[:, None] - c[None, :]), axis=1)
        counts = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors[j] = counts / counts.sum()
    return centers, priors

# 2. proximity assignment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def assign_bins(X, centers):
    """Assign every observed value to its nearest bin center.

    Returns B : (n, d) int array with the bin index in [0, nbins-1] for
    observed entries and -1 for missing entries.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        c = centers[j]
        if c is None:
            continue

            continue

        B[obs, j] = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)  # ties -> lowest index

"""Clustering evaluation of the proximity-kernel representation.

Protocol (paper Section 5.1): K-means with the number of clusters set to the
ground-truth number of classes, NMI as the metric, each experiment repeated 10
times and averaged; ``nbins`` searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.

from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]
SEEDS = list(range(10))


def evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=SEEDS, n_init=10):
    """K-means on the representation Z; returns per-seed NMI and mean/std."""
    per_seed = []
    for s in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=s)
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        per_seed.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    per_seed = np.array(per_seed)
    return {
        "per_seed": per_seed.tolist(),
        "mean": float(per_seed.mean()),
        "std": float(per_seed.std()),
        "min": float(per_seed.min()),
        "max": float(per_seed.max()),
    }


def search_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nbins_grid=NBINS_GRID, seeds=SEEDS,
                 center_mode="paper_eq4", fallback_mode="observed_only", verbose=True):
    """Search nbins by mean NMI over the 10 K-means repeats."""
    results = {}
    for nbins in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nbins, center_mode=center_mode,
                                       fallback_mode=fallback_mode)
        res = evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=seeds)
        res["nbins"] = nbins
        res["diagnostics"] = diag
        results[nbins] = res
        if verbose:
            print("nbins=%d  NMI mean=%.4f std=%.4f  (levels %s)"
                  % (nbins, res["mean"], res["std"], diag["level_counts"]), flush=True)
    best = max(results.values(), key=lambda r: r["mean"])
    return best, results

"""Reproduce claim C1 of "Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for
Incomplete Data" (arXiv:2510.13352).

Target
------
Proximity kernel ("Ours") achieves NMI 0.2289 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset
(155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes) under K-means clustering with the
ground-truth number of clusters (Table 3, row "Ours", column "Hepatitis").

Protocol (paper Section 5.1)
---------------------------
* equal-frequency binning with ``nbins`` centers per feature, taken from
  evenly-spaced percentiles of the *observed* values only (Eq. 4);
* proximity (nearest-center / Voronoi) assignment of observed values (Eq. 5);
* one-hot encoding concatenated across features (Eqs. 6-7);
* three-level cascading fallback (intersection -> union -> global prior) for
  missing entries via kernel mean embedding (Eqs. 8-14);
* K-means on the representation Z with K = ground-truth number of classes,
  NMI metric, 10 repeats averaged, ``nbins`` searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.

Usage
-----
    python reproduce.py            # full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # fast structural smoke test
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "src"))

from data import load_hepatitis  # noqa: E402
from proximity_kernel import build_representation, proximity_kernel  # noqa: E402
from cluster import evaluate_representation, search_nbins, NBINS_GRID, SEEDS  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RESULTS = os.path.join(HERE, "results")

TARGET = {
    "claim_id": "C1",
    "metric": "NMI (Normalized Mutual Information)",
    "dataset": "Hepatitis (UCI; 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes)",
    "split": "full dataset, transductive K-means clustering",
    "table_ref": "Table 3, row Ours, column Hepatitis",
    "target_value": 0.2289,
    "tolerance_absolute": 0.02,
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def structural_checks(X, y, K, nbins=2):
    """Assertions on the representation (paper Sections 4.1-4.3)."""
    n, d = X.shape
    Z, diag = build_representation(X, nbins)
    assert Z.shape == (n, d * nbins), Z.shape
    assert np.isfinite(Z).all(), "non-finite entries in Z"
    assert (Z >= 0).all() and (Z <= 1).all(), "encodings outside [0, 1]"
    # every feature encoding is a probability distribution over bins
    H = Z.reshape(n, d, nbins)
    sums = H.sum(axis=2)
    assert np.allclose(sums, 1.0, atol=1e-9), sums.min(), sums.max()
    # observed entries are exactly one-hot (R14)
    obs = ~np.isnan(X)
    onehot = H[obs]
    assert np.allclose(onehot.sum(axis=1), 1.0)
    assert set(np.unique(onehot)) <= {0.0, 1.0}
    # kernel properties (Eq. 15)
    Kmat = proximity_kernel(Z)
    assert np.allclose(Kmat, Kmat.T)
    assert (np.diag(Kmat) <= 1.0 + 1e-12).all()
    assert (Kmat >= -1e-12).all() and (Kmat <= 1.0 + 1e-12).all()
    return Z, diag


def median_imputation_baseline(X, y, K, seeds=SEEDS):
    """Sanity baseline: K-means on raw features with median imputation."""
    from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
    from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
    from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

    Ximp = SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit_transform(X)
    vals = []
    for s in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=K, init="k-means++", n_init=10, random_state=s)
        vals.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, km.fit_predict(Ximp))))
    return {"mean": float(np.mean(vals)), "per_seed": vals}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="fast structural smoke test")
    ap.add_argument("--nbins", type=int, default=None, help="restrict the nbins search")
    args = ap.parse_args()

             100.0 * np.isnan(X).sum() / X.size), flush=True)

        res = evaluate_representation(Z, y, K, seeds=[0])

    for nbins in grid:

        assert Z.shape == (n, d * nbins)
        assert np.isfinite(Z).all()
        H = Z.reshape(n, d, nbins)
        assert np.allclose(H.sum(axis=2), 1.0, atol=1e-9)
        Kmat = proximity_kernel(Z)
        assert np.allclose(Kmat, Kmat.T)
        assert (np.diag(Kmat) <= 1.0 + 1e-12).all()
        print("nbins=%d  Z=%s  missing=%d  levels=%s  K in [%.4f, %.4f]"

    print("\n--- nbins search (K-means, K=%d, %d seeds) ---" % (K, len(SEEDS)), flush=True)

target.statement: Proximity kernel ('Ours') achieves NMI 0.2289 on the Hepatitis dataset under K-means clustering with the ground-truth number of clusters.
target.dataset: Hepatitis (UCI; 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes per Table 2)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: NMI is a bounded [0,1] score on the Hepatitis dataset (155 examples, smaller than 2,000) and the paper prints values as fractions, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

audit_summary: The clean re-run recomputes C1 from the raw UCI Hepatitis file (155x19, 167/2945 = 5.67% missing, matching Table 2) in ~5 s with exit 0, and the reported 0.2289 is a genuine mean over 10 K-means seeds at the search-selected nbins=2, not a copied constant; the only occurrences of 0.2289 in the code are the target_value used for the |err| check, and the measured mean is 0.22890914 (abs err 9e-06). The pipeline implements the paper's five stages (equal-frequency percentile binning on observed values, proximity assignment, one-hot encoding, three-level cascading KME fallback, normalized inner-product kernel) and the Section 5.1 protocol (ground-truth K, NMI, 10 repeats, nbins grid {2,3,4,6,8}); R10-R12 are directly satisfied and the result is far inside the 0.02 tolerance. Two caveats for a reader: (i) the kernel is coded as (1/(d*nbins)) Z Z^T rather than the paper's (1/d) Z Z^T and is never actually used, since clustering is Euclidean K-means on Z; (ii) no timing/complexity experiment supports R13, and the O(n^2 d) fallback loop contradicts the paper's linearity claim for this implementation. Most importantly, the exact 4-decimal reproduction was achieved after the implementer searched implementation variants (center_mode paper_eq4 vs midpoint, fallback observed_only vs all_matches) and kept the variant that matched the printed table value (0.2289 vs 0.2037 for the interior-percentile variant), so the agreement is partly selection-driven even though the chosen variant is defended by the paper's min/max-center text and by A8/A14. The scale-down field is false: the full dataset, all 5 nbins values and all 10 seeds were used, and nothing in the reported number is subset or epoch limited.

requirement_check.evidence: src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins() computes bin centers per feature from obs = X[~isnan(X[:,j]), j] only, with a uniform fallback for all-missing features (A7). Repro diagnostics confirm Hepatitis missing = 167/2945 (5.67%), matching Table 2.

center_mode='paper_eq4' uses pct = 100*(k-1)/(nbins-1), k=1..nbins, np.percentile(..., method='linear'), i.e. evenly-spaced percentiles with c_{j,1}=min, c_{j,nbins}=max, as the ledger claims Eq. (4) states (A2/A13).
assign_bins() uses np.argmin(|x - c|) per observed value, ties resolved to lowest index (A3); produces Voronoi cells over centers.
encode_observed() builds H[i,j,B[i,j]]=1 and build_representation flattens to Z of shape (155, d*nbins) (e.g. 155x38 at nbins=2), the concatenated one-hot z_i.
apply_fallback() implements three ordered levels; diagnostics report level_counts {'1':61,'2':106,'3':0} at the selected nbins=2, i.e. cascading is real and executed.

Level 1: sel = inter & obs[:,j]; H[i,j] = mean one-hot of matches. Deviation from the literal Eq. (10) sum over all m in S1(i): only matches with feature j observed are averaged (A8/A14); implementer reports the 'all_matches' variant yields the same selected nbins and identical NMI at nbins=2.
Level 2 uses union |= (obs & same bin) across sample i's observed features, then means over union matches with feature j observed; exercised 106 times at nbins=2.

Level 3 assigns priors[j], the global observed bin-frequency distribution (Eq. 13), when both match sets are empty. Implemented but never triggered in this run (0 level-3 uses), so only structurally verified.

proximity_kernel() returns Z @ Z.T / Z.shape[1], i.e. 1/(d*nbins) not the paper's 1/d factor (docstring itself says d = Z.shape[1]/nbins). Constant rescaling, so rankings are unchanged, and the kernel is in any case never used downstream: clustering runs Euclidean K-means on Z directly. Kernel properties (symmetry, range, diag<=1) are asserted in structural_checks.
src/cluster.py runs sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=K) with K=2 ground-truth classes and scores with sklearn normalized_mutual_info_score; full Hepatitis set, no train/test split (A10).
SEEDS = range(10); evaluate_representation averages 10 NMI values per nbins; metrics.json stores per-seed scores (at nbins=2 all 10 are 0.22890914, std 0.0000).

NBINS_GRID = [2,3,4,6,8] is fully searched in the final run; best selected by max mean NMI -> nbins=2. Extra exploration (center_mode 'midpoint' and fallback_mode 'all_matches' via the since-deleted variants.py) was run but is not part of the reported configuration.

No complexity experiment or timing sweep over n is present; the fallback loops are per-sample over a full pairwise match mask, i.e. O(n^2 d) in the implementation, so the claimed O(nd + d n log n) linearity is neither implemented as stated nor measured.
